purpose: Determine whether replacing the v17M susceptibility curve can rescue an acceleration-screened physical metric. Prove or refute the full differentiable class q=q_base chi(A^2) with chi decreasing anywhere and a finite positive bare transverse kinetic coefficient.

authorization.allowed_outcome: retain or retire the full class of decreasing acceleration susceptibilities inside the physical matter metric

theorem.action_class: TeVeS-like derivative-disformal physical metric carried by a finite positive Einstein-aether transverse sector
theorem.assumptions: At a local background let z=v_i v_i>=0, q=q_base chi(z), q_base>0, a differentiable chi, positive reciprocal matter source J_hat=dL_m_hat/dq, and finite bare transverse kinetic coefficient K_b(z)>0 independent of the local matter amplitude.
theorem.transverse_variation: Choose delta v perpendicular to the background v. Then z(delta v)=z_0+(delta v)^2, partial q/partial delta v=0, and partial^2 q/partial(delta v)^2=2 q_base chi_prime(z_0).
theorem.exact_matter_hessian: Delta K_T=2 q_base J_hat(q) chi_prime(z_0). No L_qq term remains because the first transverse derivative of q vanishes.
theorem.zero_surface: If chi_prime(z_0)<0, J_hat_crit=K_b(z_0)/[-2 q_base chi_prime(z_0)] is finite and positive. Scaling any canonical matter realization with J_hat>0 reaches K_T=0 and then K_T<0.
theorem.mean_value_step: Any differentiable screen with chi(z_2)<chi(z_1) for z_2>z_1 has chi_prime(z_*)<0 at some z_* in (z_1,z_2). Therefore a soft start chi_prime(0)=0 relocates the zero surface but cannot remove it.
theorem.scope_limits: The theorem does not cover a constant or everywhere increasing chi, a singular infinite bare kinetic coefficient, an explicit matter-dependent compensating kinetic term, or moving the susceptibility out of the physical metric. Those are materially different mechanisms.

decision_rule: Retain curve exploration only if a differentiable curve can decrease over some acceleration interval while maintaining a positive transverse coefficient for arbitrary positive canonical matter amplitude and finite bare K_b.

If every decreasing representative has a finite positive J_hat_crit and the exact transverse Hessian identity is numerically verified, retire the complete decreasing chi(A^2) physical-metric class rather than testing more curve shapes.

Do not count the five curves as five separate physical formulations; they are witnesses to one analytic mechanism-level result. The next candidate must move environmental susceptibility outside derivative dependence of the matter metric.
